open_points.subject: administrative recovery override eligibility
open_points.text: “The administrative recovery override … is the one operation that replaces a login email; it is an exceptional flow” and INV-015 requires a “violating input” to be refused, but no rule defines what circumstances make the flow exceptional or eligible.
open_points.question: May an authorized administrator invoke the recovery override for any login-email replacement, including a routine change, or must the operation verify some recovery condition; if so, what condition and evidence?
options: Allow any authorized administrator to replace a login email, with the distinct recovery audit action providing the exceptional treatment.
Refuse unless a specified recovery condition holds, such as the holder being unable to use the existing login identifier.
Provide no ordinary email-change path and define recovery eligibility as an out-of-band administrative determination that the portal does not verify.
open_points.default_guess: Allow any authorized administrator to invoke it after normal authorization, email normalization and uniqueness checks, and distinguish it through the recovery audit action.

witness.initial: An active staff account still has a usable password and session but wants its login email changed routinely.
events: The staff holder asks an administrator for the change.
The administrator invokes perform_recovery_override with a new unique normalized email.
outcomes: The operation succeeds because recovery override is the sole email-replacement operation and no eligibility predicate is specified.
The operation is refused because the account is not in an exceptional recovery situation.
witness.observer: The administrator and staff holder see whether the email changes.

open_points.subject: security-review affected-model set
open_points.text: The security review still says authentication_credential_abuse affects “M01-M15”, while R0-23 and State 1 explicitly remove M08-M12.
open_points.question: Does “M01-M15” mean only the surviving models in that numeric span, or is the security-review evidence incomplete or invalid until its affected-model set is rewritten explicitly?
options: Interpret the range as the surviving models M01-M07 and M13-M15 only.
Treat A31 as stale and require an explicit corrected affected-model list before State 3 readiness.
Retain security-review placeholders for the removed M08-M12 concepts despite their removal from the model set.
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the range as M01-M07 and M13-M15, but rewrite it explicitly to avoid references to removed models.

witness.initial: The accepted model catalog contains M01-M07 and then M13-M15; M08-M12 do not exist.
events: A later agent materializes A31 traceability and checks whether every affected model exists.
outcomes: The agent silently skips the missing numbers and records the surviving IAM models as reviewed.
The agent treats the dangling references as an unresolved security-review error or creates obsolete placeholders for the removed models.
witness.observer: The State 3 readiness check and later security-review maintainers see different affected-model sets.
